status: SEED - reflects SHA (Social Health Authority) as of 2026; NHIF no longer exists
important: NHIF was replaced by SHA through an Act of Parliament in November 2023; SHA began operations on 1 October 2024.
All cost statements shown to patients must reference SHA and one of its three funds.
Do NOT reintroduce NHIF premium bands (KES 150-1700) anywhere in this system.

sha_overview.contributions: 2.75% of gross household monthly income, minimum KES 300 per month
sha_overview.enrolment: Mandatory for all Kenyan residents aged 18 and above
sha_overview.referral_policy: Many specialist and mental health services are directly accessible without a referral

funds.name: Primary Healthcare Fund
funds.purpose: Preventive and routine outpatient care at dispensary and health centre level
covers: Basic laboratory tests including malaria rapid diagnostic test
Primary mental health care and counselling
Wound care, suturing and tetanus vaccination
funds.patient_cost: KES 0 at dispensary and health centre level; transport is the patient's only cost

funds.name: Social Health Insurance Fund
funds.purpose: Core contributory scheme covering inpatient and specialist care
funds.patient_cost: Covered by the 2.75% contribution; a small registration fee and some medicine co-pays may apply

funds.name: Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund
covers: Cancer treatment, dialysis and organ transplant
funds.patient_cost: Fully covered - minimal to no cost to the patient

facility_levels.patient_cost_kes: covered by SHA contribution; small co-pays may apply

context_notes: The SHA transition (Oct 2024 - Apr 2025) was disrupted by system bugs and member-data migration problems, so patients may still be uncertain about their coverage. The care pathway output must state the fund in plain language.

A Ministry of Health audit in January 2026 found roughly KES 11 billion lost to fraudulent claims between October 2024 and April 2025, mostly from private hospitals. Accurate triage that right-sizes the level of care therefore has direct financial value to SHA.
Although SHA is mandatory, in practice coverage gaps still occur. If a patient's status is unknown, the system should state what the fund covers without asserting that the individual is enrolled.
sources: Social Health Insurance Act (2023) and SHA transition documentation
Ministry of Health audit findings, January 2026
